title: COP31: Bangladesh asks D-8 partners for grant climate finance
excerpt: At a D-8 ministerial session in Antalya, Bangladesh called for more grant-based and highly concessional climate finance, plus technology sharing.
content:
Bangladesh urged the D-8 group of developing countries to push for "greater access to grant-based and highly concessional climate finance" at a ministerial session on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on 17 November, Bangladesh Post reported.

Dr Saimum Parvez, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Environment, Forest and Climate Change, set out Bangladesh's climate priorities and proposed amendments to the Antalya Ministerial Action Plan. He also called for technology sharing and closer cooperation among members. He said Bangladesh plans to plant 250 million trees over five years.

The session, "From Istanbul to Antalya: D-8 Partnership in Climate Implementation", was attended by Murat Kurum, Türkiye's environment minister and COP31 President, and D-8 Secretary-General Ambassador Sohail Mahmood. Members were asked to nominate technical team representatives by 31 January 2027 for a roadmap covering 2027 to 2030.

Why it matters

Bangladesh's push for grants rather than loans runs through its COP31 positions. A D-8 roadmap could open South-South channels for technical support, though it has no new money attached so far.

What to watch

  • The final COP31 text on adaptation finance as talks close on 20 November.
  • Who Bangladesh nominates to the D-8 technical team.

Sources
